source.title_or_context: **Table I3 Core components of cardiac rehabilitation in patients with chronic obstructive lung disease.**

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms assessment, exercise, self-management, nutrition, and smoking-cessation instructions for COPD rehabilitation. A medication-specific bronchodilator instruction and an OCR-awkward oxygen-saturation threshold create mixed content requiring adjudication.

normative_assertions.notes: Spirometry/post-bronchodilator FEV1 should classify airflow limitation by the stated GOLD grades.
Symptoms should be assessed with the named tools.
COPD may be grouped A–D with exacerbation history.
Cardiopulmonary exercise testing is preferred, with the six-minute walk test additional.
Echocardiography is listed to exclude/diagnose pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

text_units.verbatim_text: Spirometry (airflow limitation should be classified based on post-bronchodilator FEV1 (GOLD grade 1 to 4)) Symptoms should be assessed based on the modified MRC dyspnoea scale, and the COPD assessment tool. Together with the history of exacerbations, COPD can be grouped in stages A to D. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (exercise capacity, differentiation of the leading cause of a reduced exercise capacity, definition of training zones based on the first ventilatory threshold) is the preferred exercise test, in addition to six minute walk test Echocardiography (exclusion/diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension; cor pulmonale)

normative_assertions.notes: The component calls for introduction to peak-flow-based self-management.

normative_assertions.notes: Exercise prescriptions should depend on capacity and COPD severity.
The programme should include the listed exercise/breathing/postural components.
Patients with measurable obstruction should use a bronchodilator before exercise.
Regular CR exercise is permitted above the stated FEV1 threshold.
Endurance exercise should be reduced by 10–15% in the stated FEV1 band.
Low-dose endurance/interval cycling and gymnastics are listed below 50%.

text_units.verbatim_text: ET prescriptions should depend on the baseline level of physical capacity and the COPD severity. The programme should include endurance (interval training), resistance exercise (especially lower body exercise), breathing exercise and instruction into postures to help shift and cough up phlegm. Patients with measurable obstruction should be advised to use a bronchodilator medication before starting the exercise. In the case of post-bronchodilator FEV1: More than 75%, the patient can be integrated into the regular CR exercise training regime Less than 75% > 50% the level of endurance exercise should be reduced by 10–15% Less than 50%, participation in low dose endurance/interval cycle ergometer training as well as gymnastics Borg-Dyspnoea-Scale value \leq 5 , breathing rate \leq 20/\text{min} is advisable Less than 30%, O 2 saturation should not exceed values less than 90%

normative_assertions.notes: The educational programme covers self-management of COPD and cardiac disease.

normative_assertions.notes: The component presents nutritional supplementation for undernutrition and COPD-related aims.

text_units.verbatim_text: Nutritional supplement therapy to improve undernutrition and to prevent progression and exacerbation of COPD and suppress inflammatory response 147

normative_assertions.notes: Smoking cessation is identified as particularly important.
All forms of smoking-cessation treatment programme should be offered.

text_units.verbatim_text: Stopping smoking is a particularly important intervention and all forms of treatment programme should be offered
